_readme: Project settings for the standards plugin hooks and the flow verifier. Edit freely; init never overwrites this file. format[].command runs from the repo root with {files} replaced by the staged files under prefix. {files} is accepted in two forms: as an unquoted word of its own in the command, or as an unquoted word of its own in the script of a sh -c or bash -c that starts a command; a word ends at a blank or at one of ; & | < > ( ) and a newline. Every other placement is refused, with a message that names the accepted forms. To pass the names into any other construct, write "$@" there and put {files} as the last word of the command. build runs in the git pre-push hook and in verify; test and mutation run in verify (mutation is a signal; empty turns it off; {files} limits it to the changed source files). build and test are a command, or a map {command, paths}: verify then runs the command only when a file changed since the base matches a path glob (** and * both cross directories), and reports it as skipped otherwise. test is also a list of {name, command, paths}, one test command each, so a change runs only the commands whose paths it touches; a command with no paths always runs. verify does not run a test command again that passed on the same command and the same files (--fresh does); a build always runs, as later checks need its outputs. protected files need [config] in the commit message. comments: line and doc are the comment tokens, public the modifier a doc comment must sit above, doc_inside the type kinds whose members may carry a doc without it (their members have no modifier), allow_markers the prefixes that make a line comment legal. gates: the project's own gates, run by the plugin hook, the git hooks and CI (check-gates.sh): {name, command, paths, when: [commit|push|ci], marker} runs command when a committed file matches a path glob (the command sees STANDARDS_COMMIT_MESSAGE and STANDARDS_STAGE; a commit whose message carries the marker skips the gate); {name, forbid: [text], marker} blocks a command that runs a text (as a word, not inside a heredoc, comment or quoted text, except sh -c, bash -c and eval) unless it carries the marker; {name, forbid_run: [program], marker} blocks only a command that starts the program (as written or by a longer path, through a shell, env, exec, nohup, nice or timeout too), never one that only names its path. project: skills (a folder; init links .claude/skills and .agents/skills to it), rules (a folder; init links .claude/rules/project to it), roster (a roster JSON in the marketplace schema; init renders it into .claude/agents/ and .codex/agents/ and installs the eval runner .standards/evals/run.sh; the review skill spawns its reviewers by paths), evals (a folder of claude plugin eval cases, one per subfolder, for the roster's agents; .standards/evals/run.sh runs them). Empty strings mean none. rules: relaxed lists the rule ids this project waives (never raised), judgement the hard or signal rule ids it grades as [judgement] (P2, declared per U-02); neither list reaches the plugin hooks, so C-01, C-02, W-01 and L-03 stay hard; re-run init after editing them, it renders the rule copies and the block from them.

format.command: for f in {files}; do sh -n -- "$f" || exit 1; done
python3 -I -c 'import ast, sys; [ast.parse(open(name, "rb").read(), name) for name in sys.argv[1:]]' {files}
